roadmap.title: Full Stack Developer at a climate tech startup
roadmap.summary: Build practical full-stack web and cloud skills (React, Node, Postgres, Docker, AWS) plus climate-domain projects to win early-stage climate-tech hires.

nodes.title: Git & GitHub basics
nodes.why: Version control and basic Git/GitHub workflows are required for nearly every developer interview and collaboration.

nodes.title: HTML, CSS, responsive layout
nodes.why: Frontend markup and responsive design are expected skills for any full-stack candidate building web UIs.

nodes.title: JavaScript (ES6+) fundamentals
nodes.why: Modern full-stack development at startups is driven by JavaScript across frontend and backend.

nodes.title: React + hooks & state
nodes.why: Most climate-tech startups use React (or similar) for building interactive dashboards and tools.

nodes.title: Node.js & Express APIs
nodes.why: Backend API development with Node/Express is a common stack for rapid product iterations in startups.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL & SQL modeling
nodes.why: Relational data modeling and SQL (Postgres) are essential for storing sensor and emissions datasets used in climate apps.

nodes.title: API auth & security
nodes.why: Understanding JWTs, OAuth basics and securing APIs is required for production-ready features and interviews.

nodes.title: GraphQL basics (Apollo)
nodes.why: GraphQL is commonly used for efficient data fetching in SPAs; it’s useful but not strictly required at all startups.

nodes.title: Docker containerization
nodes.why: Containerizing apps with Docker is expected in modern deployments and for reproducible developer environments.

nodes.title: AWS fundamentals (EC2, S3, RDS)
nodes.why: Many startups host services on AWS; you must know S3, RDS, EC2 and basic IAM to deploy and debug apps.

nodes.title: Infrastructure as Code (Terraform)
nodes.why: Terraform helps automate cloud infra which is valuable for startups scaling, but smaller teams sometimes use simpler tooling.

nodes.title: Testing & CI (Jest, GitHub Actions)
nodes.why: Unit/integration tests and CI pipelines are expected to ship reliable features and appear in many junior role descriptions.

nodes.title: Project: Emissions dashboard (Mapbox)
nodes.why: A public dashboard that visualizes emissions or energy metrics using Mapbox and real datasets demonstrates domain relevance and full-stack chops.

nodes.title: Project: IoT sensor data pipeline
nodes.why: Building a pipeline ingesting time-series sensor data (MQTT -> API -> DB) mirrors real climate-tech problems and impresses employers.

nodes.title: AWS Certified Developer - Associate
nodes.why: This certification validates practical AWS skills; useful at startups that value cloud competence but not required for every junior role.

nodes.title: Apply & interview prep (roles)
nodes.why: Preparing tailored applications, coding challenges, and behavioral answers is necessary to convert technical ability into job offers.

roadmap.title: UI/UX Designer for fintech apps
roadmap.summary: A focused roadmap to become a UI/UX designer who builds secure, compliant, usable fintech mobile and web products.

nodes.title: UX fundamentals
nodes.why: Understanding core UX principles (usability, affordance, heuristics) is required for designing clear fintech experiences.

nodes.title: Visual design basics
nodes.why: Typography, color, spacing and composition determine trust and readability in finance interfaces.

nodes.title: Interaction & motion basics
nodes.why: Micro-interactions and flow clarity reduce user errors in payment and transaction flows.

nodes.title: UX research methods
nodes.why: User interviews, surveys and usability testing reveal trust and security concerns specific to finance users.

nodes.title: Information architecture
nodes.why: Fintech apps need clear organization of accounts, transactions and settings to prevent costly user errors.

nodes.title: Figma prototyping & components
nodes.why: Figma is the industry standard for building interactive fintech prototypes and reusable component libraries.

nodes.title: Design systems & tokens
nodes.why: Design systems scale UI consistency across complex fintech products and speed handoff to engineers.

nodes.title: Moderated usability testing
nodes.why: Running tests on payment and onboarding flows surfaces real user friction in fintech contexts.

nodes.title: Financial data visualization
nodes.why: Designing clear charts and statements is key for account summaries, portfolio views and transaction insights.

nodes.title: Security & privacy UX
nodes.why: Designing clear consent, MFA and fraud flows is essential to user trust and regulatory needs in fintech.

nodes.title: Mobile banking app project
nodes.why: A polished end-to-end mobile banking prototype (onboarding, KYC, transfers, statements) is a core fintech portfolio piece.

nodes.title: KYC & onboarding flow
nodes.why: Designing KYC flows demonstrates ability to balance conversion, compliance and UX — a fintech hiring must-have.

nodes.title: Google UX Design Certificate
nodes.why: A recognized certificate that validates practical UX workflow skills useful in entry-level fintech interviews.

nodes.title: Portfolio & case studies
nodes.why: Concise fintech case studies with metrics and prototypes are required to get interviews for UI/UX fintech roles.

nodes.title: Apply for design internships
nodes.why: Internships at fintech startups or banks provide product experience and domain context for future hires.

nodes.title: Apply to entry-level roles
nodes.why: Applying and interviewing for junior UI/UX designer roles in fintech is the final step to get hired.

roadmap.title: Data Analyst in healthcare
roadmap.summary: A practical roadmap to become an entry-level healthcare data analyst by building core analytics skills, healthcare data knowledge, domain-specific tools (SQL, Power BI/Tableau, Python/R), compliant workflows, and a portfolio of healthcare projects.

nodes.title: Advanced Excel (pivot, power query)
nodes.why: Hiring managers expect strong spreadsheet skills for cleaning, exploratory analysis, and quick ad-hoc healthcare reports.

nodes.title: Applied statistics for analytics
nodes.why: Understanding distributions, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals and effect sizes is essential to interpret clinical and claims data correctly.

nodes.title: SQL for analysts (Postgres/MySQL)
nodes.why: Most healthcare data lives in relational databases; SQL is the primary language to extract patient cohorts and aggregate measures.

nodes.title: Python + pandas for data cleaning
nodes.why: Python with pandas accelerates reproducible cleaning, merging of clinical datasets, and lightweight analysis beyond spreadsheets.

nodes.title: Power BI or Tableau desktop
nodes.why: Data visualization tools are required to create operational dashboards used by clinicians and administrators in healthcare settings.

nodes.title: ICD-10, CPT, RxNorm basics
nodes.why: Coding systems like ICD-10 and CPT are foundational to interpret diagnoses, procedures and claims data common in healthcare analytics.

nodes.title: HIPAA & PHI handling
nodes.why: Any analyst working with patient-level data must know HIPAA privacy rules and secure handling of protected health information.

nodes.title: FHIR & HL7 overview
nodes.why: Understanding FHIR/HL7 helps when extracting clinical data from EHR systems or working with interoperability teams.

nodes.title: Google Data Analytics Certificate
nodes.why: This certificate validates core analytics workflow skills for employers and helps structure early projects and resumes.

nodes.title: EHR cohort analysis (MIMIC-III)
nodes.why: A reproducible cohort analysis using the MIMIC public ICU dataset demonstrates ability to work with real clinical data and answer clinical questions.

nodes.title: Claims cost and utilization dashboard
nodes.why: Payor/provider roles often ask for experience summarizing claims (CPT/ICD) and utilization trends via dashboards.

nodes.title: Risk stratification prototype (basic ML)
nodes.why: A simple logistic regression model for readmission risk shows familiarity with predictive analytics used in population health teams.

nodes.title: Healthcare data governance basics
nodes.why: Hospitals and payors expect analysts to follow governance policies for lineage, de-identification and approved use of patient data.

nodes.title: Apply: healthcare analyst internship
nodes.why: An internship provides supervised experience with EHR/claims systems and makes your resume competitive for entry-level hires.

nodes.title: Apply: entry-level healthcare data analyst
nodes.why: Applying and interviewing for junior analyst roles is the final step to transition into a healthcare analytics position.

nodes.title: Tableau Desktop Specialist
nodes.why: A Tableau certification can differentiate you when the role emphasizes visualization and dashboard delivery in health systems.
